reference_use.conclusion: The snapshot (project d8d46c95, Mathlib 25730c7c) contains the frozen Ch06 Contract; Submission is byte-identical, so child statements may use only contract, SimonGMT and Mathlib names. SimonGMT provides currents with sequential continuity, boundary, massOn (Euclidean coefficient norm), support/zeroRegion and the vector Riesz theorem `simon_theorem_4_14` on any locally compact Hausdorff space (Radon outer measure, unit field a.e.). It has only linear co-area and no co-area for rectifiable sets, and Mathlib has neither (nor Lusin's continuity theorem), so these are cited from Simon Ch. 3 §2 and Ch. 1, 1.17. Mathlib provides McShane (`LipschitzOnWith.extend_real`), Rademacher (`LipschitzOnWith.ae_differentiableWithinAt_of_mem`), Lebesgue's theorem for monotone functions (`Monotone.ae_differentiableAt`, `MonotoneOn.intervalIntegral_deriv_mem_uIcc`) and π-system uniqueness of finite measures (`ext_of_generate_finite`). In a scratch build of the frozen project, all six child statements elaborate in the comparator's child scope. `SlicingTheorem` follows from the four property children by `choose` plus assembly. `slicing_exists` follows from `slicing_mass_representation`, `slicing_support_subset` from `slicing_representation_unique`, and the restriction-mass identification used by `slicing_mass_bound` from both. All of these are kernel-checked with axioms [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]. The DAG (20 nodes) reserves none of the six proposed names; the concurrently added polyhedral children have different names and types. These checks do not certify the analytic proofs.

subproblem.title: Support of slices (Simon 4.8)
subproblem.statement: For all P, m, every open U ⊆ ℝ^P, every T ∈ D_{m+1}(U), every f : ℝ^P → ℝ which is L-Lipschitz on U, every t ∈ ℝ and every S ∈ D_m(U) with IsSlice T f t S: spt S ⊆ spt T ∩ {x : f(x) = t} (supports in the sense of GeometricCurrentOn.support, relative to U).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)), IsOpen U → ∀ T : GeometricCurrentOn U (m + 1), ∀ (f : Eucl P → ℝ) (L : ℝ≥0), LipschitzOnWith L f U → ∀ (t : ℝ) (S : GeometricCurrentOn U m), IsSlice T f t S → S.support ⊆ T.support ∩ {x | f x = t}
subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions (as in the parent proof). D^k(U) is the space of test k-forms on U (smooth, compact support, tsupport ⊆ U; `TestFormOn U k`), D_k(U) the currents (`GeometricCurrentOn U k`: linear, and X(ω_j) → 0 whenever ω_j → 0 in D^k(U), i.e. all tsupports lie in one compact K ⊆ U and every iterated derivative of ω_j tends to 0 uniformly on K). I(k,P) is the set of strictly increasing β : {1,…,k} → {1,…,P}; e_β := (e_{β_1},…,e_{β_k}); dx^β is the coordinate k-covector, dx^β(e_γ) = δ_{βγ} for β, γ ∈ I(k,P). Fact A: every k-covector α equals Σ_β α(e_β) dx^β, and |α|² = Σ_β α(e_β)², where |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α. A k-vector is a continuous linear functional w on k-covectors (`NVector`); put w^β := w(dx^β), so w(α) = Σ_β α(e_β) w^β and |w(α)| ≤ |α|·|w| with |w| := (Σ_β (w^β)²)^{1/2} (Cauchy–Schwarz). For a form ω, ‖ω‖ := sup_x |ω(x)|. M_W(X) = X.massOn W is the supremum of X(ω) over ω ∈ D^k(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x. ρ_ε is a standard mollifier (smooth, ≥ 0, supported in the closed ε-ball, ∫ρ_ε = 1); for a continuous compactly supported form φ, ρ_ε*φ (componentwise convolution) is smooth, supported in the closed ε-neighbourhood of tsupport φ, satisfies |ρ_ε*φ(x)| ≤ ‖φ‖ (|·| is a norm, hence convex) and ρ_ε*φ → φ uniformly as ε ↓ 0. All measures are Borel measures on ℝ^P = Eucl P.

Source: Simon Ch. 6, 4.8 and the parent proof's Step 2 (a)–(c), with the parent's locality R4 replaced by the sibling `slicing_representation_unique` (applied to the representations supplied by IsSlice). Let P, m, U open, T ∈ D_{m+1}(U), f : ℝ^P → ℝ L-Lipschitz on U, t ∈ ℝ and S ∈ D_m(U) with IsSlice T f t S. Write A_t := {x | x ∈ U ∧ f x < t}.

0. (Unpacking IsSlice.) There are currents A ∈ D_{m+1}(U), B ∈ D_m(U), Borel measures μ, μ′ and maps v, v′ with: IsMeasureRepresentation T μ v and A(η) = ∫_{A_t} v(η) dμ for all η ∈ D^{m+1}(U); IsMeasureRepresentation ∂T μ′ v′ and B(ω) = ∫_{A_t} v′(ω) dμ′ for all ω ∈ D^m(U); and S(ω) = ∂A(ω) − B(ω) = A(dω) − B(ω). Since tsupport dω ⊆ tsupport ω (`tsupport_exteriorDerivative_subset`), for every ω ∈ D^m(U):
 (*) S(ω) = ∫_{A_t} v(x)(dω(x)) dμ − ∫_{A_t} v′(x)(ω(x)) dμ′, with T(dω) = ∫ v(dω) dμ = ∂T(ω) = ∫ v′(ω) dμ′.

1. (What must be shown.) S.support = U ∖ zeroRegion(S), where zeroRegion(S) is the union of the open sets W′ with compact closure ⊆ U on which S vanishes (S(ω) = 0 whenever tsupport ω ⊆ W′). Let x ∈ S.support: x ∈ U and S vanishes on no open W′ ∋ x with compact closure ⊆ U. We show x ∈ T.support and f(x) = t by exhibiting, in each contrary case, such a W′ ∋ x on which S vanishes.

2. (x ∈ T.support; parent Step 2(c).) Suppose x ∈ zeroRegion(T): x ∈ W′ open, closure W′ compact ⊆ U, and T(η) = 0 for every η ∈ D^{m+1}(U) with tsupport η ⊆ W′. Then ∂T(ω) = T(dω) = 0 whenever tsupport ω ⊆ W′. Apply `slicing_representation_unique` with degree m+1, (μ₁, v₁) := (μ, v), (μ₂, v₂) := (0, 0) and the open set W′: the integrability hypotheses hold (IsMeasureRepresentation; anything is integrable for the zero measure) and ∫ v(η) dμ = T(η) = 0 = ∫ 0 d0 for tsupport η ⊆ W′; it yields ∫_{A_t} v(η) dμ = 0 for every η ∈ D^{m+1}(U) with tsupport η ⊆ W′. Likewise in degree m with (μ′, v′), (0, 0), W′: ∫_{A_t} v′(ω) dμ′ = 0 whenever tsupport ω ⊆ W′. By (*) with η = dω, S(ω) = 0 whenever tsupport ω ⊆ W′; so S vanishes on W′ ∋ x, a contradiction. Hence x ∉ zeroRegion(T), and with x ∈ U, x ∈ T.support.

3. (f(x) = t; parent Step 2(a),(b).) f is continuous at x (continuous on the open set U ∋ x).
 (a) If f(x) < t, there is r > 0 with B(x,r) ⊆ U and f < t on B(x,r). Let W′ := B(x, r/2); it is open, its closure is the closed ball of radius r/2, compact and ⊆ B(x,r) ⊆ U. If tsupport ω ⊆ W′, then tsupport dω ⊆ tsupport ω ⊆ A_t, so the integrands in (*) vanish off A_t and ∫_{A_t} v(dω) dμ = ∫ v(dω) dμ = T(dω), ∫_{A_t} v′(ω) dμ′ = ∫ v′(ω) dμ′ = ∂T(ω) = T(dω); hence S(ω) = 0. So S vanishes on W′ ∋ x, a contradiction.
 (b) If f(x) > t, there is r > 0 with B(x,r) ⊆ U and f > t on B(x,r); let W′ := B(x, r/2) as before. If tsupport ω ⊆ W′, then tsupport dω and tsupport ω are disjoint from A_t, so both integrands in (*) vanish on A_t and S(ω) = 0 − 0 = 0. Again a contradiction.
 Hence f(x) = t.

4. (Conclusion.) Every x ∈ S.support lies in T.support ∩ {x | f x = t}, i.e. spt S ⊆ spt T ∩ {f = t} (Simon 4.8). ∎
proof_key_steps: Unpack IsSlice: S(ω) = ∫_{A_t} v(dω) dμ − ∫_{A_t} v′(ω) dμ′ with representations (μ, v) of T and (μ′, v′) of ∂T.
If T vanishes on an open W′ ⊂⊂ U, so does ∂T; slicing_representation_unique with the zero representation kills both restricted integrals for forms supported in W′, so S vanishes on W′.
If f(x) < t, on a small ball inside {f < t} both restricted integrals equal T(dω), so S vanishes there.
If f(x) > t, on a small ball inside {f > t} both restricted integrals vanish, so S vanishes there.
Hence every point of spt S lies in spt T and has f = t.

audit.reason: The stronger statement without explicit mass hypotheses is justified by the representations already supplied by IsSlice. Local uniqueness against the zero representation handles points outside T.support; cancellation below the level and vanishing above it handle the remaining points. The argument matches the frozen relative-support definition and uses only representation_unique.
